label: English · 204 words
text: Dr. Tomaz Amorim is the Principal Investigator of subproject TP 4, “Extractivism and Infrastructure in Brazilian Literature”, of DFG Research Unit FOR 5710 “Infrastructure: Aesthetics and Supply” at Ruhr-Universität Bochum. He is an Associated Investigator at the Maria Sibylla Merian Centre Conviviality-Inequality in Latin America (Mecila), where he previously served as Academic Coordinator. He is also an Associated Researcher and member of the Executive Board at the Brazilian Center for Analysis and Planning (CEBRAP). He obtained his PhD in 2018 in Literary Theory and Comparative Literature at the University of São Paulo (USP) with a thesis on Franz Kafka and Walter Benjamin (Contar do tempo interrompido / Narrating Interrupted Time), which included a research stay at the Humboldt University of Berlin. Following his doctorate, he was a Postdoctoral Researcher at Unicamp, where he researched non-modern interfaces in Oswald de Andrade and Walter Benjamin, and a Fellow at the Cluster of Excellence Temporal Communities: Doing Literature in a Global Perspective at the Freie Universität Berlin. As a writer and critic, he published the volume Arquipélago: literatura brasileira contemporânea (2023) as well as the poetry collections Plástico pluma (2018) and Meia-lua soco (2020). His current research project investigates the aesthetic configurations of extractivism in Brazilian literature.

label: Português · 105 palavras
text: Tomaz Amorim é crítico literário e pesquisador especializado em literatura brasileira moderna e contemporânea, frequentemente em diálogo comparativo com a literatura alemã e a Teoria Crítica. Atualmente, é Pesquisador Principal do subprojeto TP 4, “Extractivism and Infrastructure in Brazilian Literature”, da Unidade de Pesquisa DFG FOR 5710 “Infrastructure: Aesthetics and Supply”, na Ruhr-Universität Bochum (Alemanha), e Pesquisador Associado no Mecila (Maria Sibylla Merian Centre Conviviality-Inequality in Latin America), onde atuou anteriormente como Coordenador Acadêmico. É doutor em Teoria Literária e Literatura Comparada pela Universidade de São Paulo (USP), título obtido em 2018 com a tese Franz Kafka e Walter Benjamin: narrar o tempo interrompido.
